articles.title: Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases as it reaches Kenya and Nigeria
articles.body:
A large Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has now passed 10,000 confirmed cases, and has spread to Kenya and Nigeria. In its latest update on 6 November 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) said no new cases had been found in Kenya or Nigeria since its previous report.

Ebola is a severe and often deadly disease that spreads through contact with the body fluids of sick people. This outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, one type of Ebola virus.

## How big is the outbreak?

The outbreak in the DRC was declared in May 2026. As of 3 November, WHO reported:

- 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths, almost all in the DRC. About half of confirmed patients have died.
- Cases in 67 health zones across eight provinces. Ituri province, in the east, is the worst hit.
- 964 new cases and 511 deaths in about two weeks.

WHO said many deaths are happening in communities rather than in clinics, and that contact tracing in some areas is below its target. Contact tracing means finding and checking people who were near a sick person.

## Kenya and Nigeria

Kenya has 9 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, all in Nairobi. The first case was a man who travelled from the DRC through Uganda and flew to Nairobi on 3 October. The other eight were family members and health workers linked to him. There have been no new cases since 19 October, and contact monitoring is due to end on 11 November.

Nigeria confirmed one case on 20 October in Abuja, the capital. The patient had travelled from Uganda and was later flown to Geneva, Switzerland, for treatment. Officials are still investigating how the person was infected, and 62 contacts have been identified.

Earlier outbreaks linked to this one in Uganda and France have been brought under control.

## Vaccines and treatment

WHO says there are no approved vaccines or specific medicines for the Bundibugyo virus. On 23 October, a large trial of candidate vaccines, called Tumaini, began in Bunia in the DRC. WHO experts also recommended adding two more candidates, from Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and from Moderna.

## Risk and advice

WHO rates the risk as very high in the DRC, high for neighbouring countries and low for the rest of Africa and the world, but says it is updating this assessment. WHO advises against limits on travel or trade with affected countries.

Sources: World Health Organization, ECDC, Al Jazeera, NPR

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: Tanzania's opposition leader Lissu cleared of treason, jailed 4 years
articles.body:
A court in Tanzania cleared opposition leader Tundu Lissu of treason on Friday, 6 November 2026, but found him guilty of incitement and sentenced him to four years in prison. Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, and in Tanzania it can carry the death penalty.

Lissu, 58, is the chairman of Chadema, Tanzania's main opposition party. Tanzania is a country of East Africa, on the Indian Ocean coast.

## The case

Lissu was arrested in April 2025 and charged with treason. The charge was based on a speech in which, prosecutors said, he told supporters the opposition would "block the election" and "mobilise rebellion."

The court said prosecutors had not given enough evidence to prove treason. But it convicted him of incitement, meaning encouraging others to break the law. Lissu pleaded not guilty, saying his speech broke no law and that the case was political. After the ruling, he objected that he had been charged with treason, not with a separate incitement offence.

Police surrounded the courtroom in Dar es Salaam, the country's largest city, before the verdict, and crowds gathered nearby.

## Reactions

- Chadema said Lissu will appeal against the sentence.
- Amnesty International, a human rights group, called the verdict a travesty of justice and called for his release.
- US Ambassador William Trachman said Washington was following the trial closely because of its "broader implications for the rule of law."
- The government rejects accusations of a crackdown on critics.

## Background: the 2025 election

Lissu's arrest came before Tanzania's general election in October 2025. Chadema was barred from taking part. Rights groups also accused the authorities of abducting government critics. These issues helped fuel protests during the vote, which became the worst political unrest in Tanzania's history.

Police fired on protesters in several cities. A commission set up by President Samia Suluhu Hassan said in April 2026 that at least 518 people were killed, and blamed protesters for the violence. Human rights groups say security forces used too much force. The government denies this. Hassan was declared the winner of the election with nearly 98 percent of the vote.

Lissu has a long history in Tanzanian politics. He survived being shot 16 times in an attack in 2017, and no one has been charged. He lived in exile, ran for president in 2020 and came second, then returned home in 2023 after Hassan eased restrictions on the opposition.

Sources: CNBC Africa (Reuters), AP, The Citizen, Monitor

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: AI and Chip Stocks Fall Sharply After US Midterm Elections
articles.body:
Shares in AI chip makers and data-centre companies fell sharply on Thursday, 5 November 2026. Investors were worried that the results of the US midterm elections could bring stricter rules for AI and slow the building of new data centres.

## What happened in the markets

Democrats won control of both houses of the US Congress in the elections on 3 November. Markets rose strongly on 4 November, but on 5 November technology shares dropped. According to CNBC and Fortune:

- The Nasdaq index, which contains many tech companies, fell about 5%.
- Nvidia fell 9.3%, AMD fell 17.3% and Micron fell 17.5%.
- "Neocloud" companies, which rent out AI computing power, were hit hard. Nebius fell 15%, IREN 17% and CoreWeave 10%.
- The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which follows chip companies, had one of its worst days since March 2020.

Shares began to recover on Friday, 6 November. Some analysts called the fall a "knee-jerk reaction", meaning a sudden reaction without careful thought.

## Votes against data centres

Data centres are large buildings full of computers that train and run AI. They use a lot of electricity and water, and some local communities oppose them.

- Fortune reported that 41 local ballot measures aimed at slowing data-centre building were voted on, and that most passed, especially in Ohio.
- In Texas, which Wells Fargo estimates has 27% of planned US data-centre capacity, Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor. She has called for a pause on new data centres. Governor Greg Abbott had already paused new data-centre permits in September while the power grid was reviewed.

## Pressure on the building boom

The fall came after a difficult October for AI shares, with worries about high spending and interest rates. Goldman Sachs estimates that AI-related spending on computers, data centres and power could reach about $7.6 trillion from 2026 to 2031.

On the same day, IREN, an Australian data-centre company, said some deliveries for Microsoft would be delayed because Microsoft asked for network design changes. IREN said there would be no financial penalties.

An analyst at Barclays said that because electricity is scarce, the biggest companies with the most money will have an advantage. He called it "a war of attrition", meaning a long contest where the strongest survive.

Sources: CNBC, Fortune, Reuters

articles.title: US Justice Department sets up a task force to fight misuse of AI
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
The US Department of Justice has created a new team to deal with crimes and other abuses that use artificial intelligence (AI). It is called the Super Intelligence Task Force. The department announced it on 5 November 2026.

## Who leads it

Attorney General Todd Blanche, the top US law officer, set up the team in a memo dated 13 October. Two senior officials will lead it: Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward and Associate Deputy Attorney General Stephen Weiss.

The name uses the term "super intelligence." In late September, President Donald Trump signed an order telling government agencies to use "super intelligence" instead of "artificial intelligence."

## What it will do

The task force will try to stop AI being misused by:

- foreign governments and groups working for them
- international criminal gangs
- companies or people who use AI for fraud or other crimes

It will also:

- organise the department's criminal and civil cases involving AI
- suggest which AI-related offences should be a priority
- write guidance for prosecutors on how to charge illegal AI-related conduct
- take over the work of an earlier team, the AI Litigation Task Force, created in January 2026

Reports say the task force also wants AI companies to improve their internal controls and risk reporting, so that their models "behave as intended."

Blanche wrote that the aim is to make sure "America's leadership in SI is not compromised by the misuse of SI." Here, SI means super intelligence. The team is also meant to support what he called American "SI dominance."

## Link to the White House

Last month, President Trump announced a separate group called the Super Intelligence Force. It is led by Jay Clayton, the Director of National Intelligence, who now handles AI for the White House. That group coordinates the government's work with AI companies and other organisations.

The Justice Department's new team will be its main contact with that group. Blanche said it will help make sure that important AI technology serves the American people and is "not manipulated by bad actors at home or abroad."

## What is still unclear

The department did not give a timeline for the task force's work. It also did not explain in detail how it will work with other government agencies.

Sources: Nextgov, US Department of Justice, Decrypt

articles.title: US voters approve dozens of local limits on new data centres
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
In the US midterm elections on 3 November 2026, voters in many towns and cities approved new limits on data centres. A data centre is a large building full of computers. Companies are building many of them to run artificial intelligence (AI) services.

## How many measures passed?

According to Ballotpedia, a US election information website, there were 41 local data centre measures on the ballot in 10 states. Of these, 28 aimed to restrict data centres and 13 aimed to support new projects.

Counts of how many restrictions passed differ between sources and grew as votes were counted. The Washington Post reported at least 29 places, while other outlets reported 33 or 38. Bisnow reported that all but one of the proposed restrictions passed.

The measures included:

- full bans on new data centres
- temporary pauses, called moratoriums, of up to six months
- rules that require voters to approve new projects
- limits on very large centres, for example those using more than 25 megawatts of power

## Examples

- Alhambra, California: about 82% voted for a citywide ban on building data centres.
- Edgewater, Florida: 77% voted to ban new data centres.
- Bloomington, Illinois: nearly 78% backed a non-binding call for a temporary pause on large projects.
- Ohio had the most votes on the issue, with 21 measures.

## Why people are worried

Data centres use large amounts of electricity and water. Many residents fear higher power bills, pressure on local power grids, noise and harm to the environment. An NBC News exit poll found that 56% of voters said AI and data centres were a "crucial" or "major" factor in how they voted for Congress.

The issue also played a role in races for state governor. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Governor Greg Abbott after promising a statewide pause until stronger rules are in place. In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms won after campaigning for a temporary pause and an end to tax breaks for data centres.

## What it means for the AI industry

Some people in the industry expect more delays and higher costs for new projects. A data centre construction consultant said he may lower his building forecasts for 2027. Shares of some smaller data centre companies fell after the vote.

Sources: Anadolu Agency, Bisnow, Ballotpedia, The Washington Post

articles.title: Google plans $15 billion investment in Malaysia's data centres
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Google says it will invest $15 billion (about 61 billion Malaysian ringgit) in Malaysia in 2027 and 2028. The company announced the plan on 4 November 2026. The money will go to data centres, clean energy, water supply and training for workers.

## What Google will build

A data centre is a large building full of computers that store data and run online services, including AI.

- Google will expand its first Malaysian campus at Elmina Business Park in Selangor, which is already running.
- It will build new campuses in Selangor and in Negeri Sembilan. Reports say the Negeri Sembilan site is in Port Dickson.
- The Selangor sites will also support a planned Google Cloud region in Malaysia. No start date has been given.

This is much larger than Google's earlier plan, announced in May 2024, to invest $2 billion in Malaysia.

## Jobs and the economy

Google estimates that:

- During building work, the project will add about $1.1 billion a year to Malaysia's economy and support more than 37,000 local jobs each year.
- Once the centres are running, they will support more than 9,000 local jobs a year, with wages on average 45% above the national median.

These are Google's own estimates.

## Power and water

Data centres use a lot of electricity and water, which worries people in many countries. Google says it will:

- help add more than 1 gigawatt of clean energy to Malaysia's power grid
- pay for all the electricity its campuses use and the direct costs of connecting them to the grid
- fund a separate $160 million reservoir and water treatment plant in Negeri Sembilan, which reports say will supply 65 million litres of treated water a day

## Training

Google plans four new programmes to train 800,000 Malaysians over five years.

Ruth Porat, president and chief investment officer of Alphabet, Google's parent company, said the investment "aligns with Malaysia's development priorities." Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim attended the announcement, reports say.

## Why it matters

Malaysia has become one of Southeast Asia's main centres for data centres, as big technology companies race to build computing power for AI. The project could bring jobs and investment, but it will also add to demand for power and water.

Sources: The Star (Reuters), Google, Malay Mail, DataCenterDynamics

articles.title: Suez Canal has its busiest month since the Red Sea crisis began
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Egypt's Suez Canal had its busiest month in three years in October 2026. The head of the Suez Canal Authority (SCA), Osama Rabie, gave the figures on Thursday, November 5.

The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea. It is one of the most important shipping routes between Asia and Europe, and its fees are a major source of foreign currency for Egypt.

## The October numbers

According to the SCA, in October 2026:

- 1,490 ships passed through the canal.
- Their combined net tonnage was 88 million tons. Net tonnage is a measure of a ship's cargo space.
- The canal earned $724 million in revenue.

Compared with October 2025, the number of ships rose by 32%, net tonnage rose by 86%, and revenue rose by 94%. In October 2025 the canal handled 1,128 ships and earned $373 million, according to Egyptian media reports.

Egyptian officials said this was the highest monthly traffic since the Red Sea crisis began in late 2023.

## Why traffic fell before

Since November 2023, security concerns in the Red Sea have led many shipping companies to avoid the area. Instead, their ships sailed around the Cape of Good Hope at the southern tip of Africa. That trip is much longer and more expensive, but it avoided the risk of attacks near Yemen. As a result, canal traffic and Egypt's income from the canal dropped sharply.

## A slow return

Traffic has been recovering through 2026. In September, a Ports Europe report said weekly traffic had reached its highest level since early 2024.

Rabie said he is optimistic. He expects the rise to continue as "most international shipping lines resume transits". He said the recovery shows the canal's role in supporting global supply chains "despite regional geopolitical challenges".

Earlier, the SCA chairman said he hoped canal income could reach about $8 billion in Egypt's 2026/27 financial year. It is not yet clear whether that target will be met.

Sources: Xinhua via The Star, Ahram Online, Egypt Today, Ports Europe

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: Nintendo profit rises as Switch 2 passes 26 million consoles sold
articles.body:
Japanese game company Nintendo reported its results for April to September 2026 on November 5. Its profit went up, even though it sold fewer Switch 2 consoles than in the same period last year.

## The main numbers

- Net sales (total money from sales) were 966 billion yen, down 12.1% from a year earlier.
- Net profit was 220.9 billion yen, up 11.0%.
- Reports say operating profit, the profit from the main business, was 216.5 billion yen, up 49.1%.

Nintendo sold 6.49 million Switch 2 consoles in the six months. A year earlier, in the months just after the console launched in June 2025, it sold 10.36 million. That is a fall of about 37% to 40%, depending on how outlets calculate it.

In total, Nintendo has now sold 26.35 million Switch 2 consoles worldwide, as of September 30, 2026. The original Switch, released in 2017, is still selling too.

## Why profit went up

Reports give three main reasons:

- Games made up a bigger share of sales. Games usually earn more profit than consoles.
- Nintendo got back money it had paid in US import taxes (tariffs) earlier, which helped its costs.
- Income from its characters and brands rose about 90%, helped by the film The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.

## Best-selling games

Switch 2 game sales in the half year were 24.49 million copies, up 18.8%. Mario Kart World is the top Switch 2 game, with about 16.48 million copies sold in total. Donkey Kong Bananza has passed 5 million.

Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream, a life-simulation game released for the original Switch in April 2026, sold 8.81 million copies.

## Looking ahead

Nintendo kept its forecast of selling 16.5 million Switch 2 consoles in the full financial year, which ends in March 2027.

Some outlets give slightly different numbers for the drop in console sales. Nintendo's own report is the official source for all figures.

Sources: Nippon.com (Jiji Press), Games.gg, Thurrott

articles.title: Turkey Approves the Mecca Defence Pact With Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
In early November 2026, Turkey's parliament approved the "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement", a military pact between Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. The vote was 279 in favour and 119 against. It clears the way for Turkey to send military support to Saudi Arabia, which is under attack from Yemen's Houthis.

Reports give slightly different days for the vote. Al-Monitor said it took place on Wednesday, November 4, while other reports said Thursday.

## What the pact says

The three countries signed the agreement on August 7, 2026. It has 16 articles. The main points, as reported by Al Jazeera and Reuters:

- An armed attack on one member is treated as an attack on all three. This is similar to Article 5 of NATO, the Western military alliance.
- Each country decides how much help to give, and what kind.
- The members will cooperate on the defence industry, share intelligence, train together and fight terrorism.
- A committee of the foreign and defence ministers of all three countries will manage it.
- Other countries can join only if all three founding members agree.
- The pact lasts 10 years. After that, any member can leave.

## Why it matters now

On October 5, after Houthi missiles and drones hit Saudi airports and oil sites, officials from the three countries met in Riyadh. They agreed to start "deterrence measures" under the pact and to send forces to the kingdom quickly. Pakistan said its role includes support tasks such as reconnaissance (watching and gathering information).

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said in October: "we are surrounded by a ring of fire."

## Will Turkish troops go to Saudi Arabia?

Not automatically. Any deployment of Turkish soldiers needs a separate vote in parliament. No deployment has been announced. Defence Minister Yasar Guler said Turkey's aim "would be to strengthen deterrence" and added: "We absolutely do not foresee entering into any conflict with the Houthis." Al-Monitor reported that Turkish help is more likely to be training, advice and equipment than a large number of troops.

Opposition parties, including the Yeni Party and the pro-Kurdish DEM Party, voted against. They said the deal could pull Turkey into regional wars.

## Could Syria join?

Syria's foreign minister, Asaad al-Shaibani, said in early November that talks were "under way" about Syria joining the alliance. No decision has been announced.

Sources: Al-Monitor, Al Jazeera, Reuters, Cyprus Mail, TRT World

articles.title: Goldman Sachs and Apple put new limits on staff use of AI tools
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Two of the world's biggest companies have reduced how much their staff can use AI tools. In early November 2026, Bloomberg reported that the bank Goldman Sachs has limited advanced AI coding tools to its engineers, and that Apple has cut daily AI spending limits for its workers.

## Goldman Sachs: coding tools for engineers only

Goldman Sachs is a large US investment bank. According to Bloomberg, which saw internal guidance updated in October:

- Most traders and bankers can no longer use advanced AI coding tools such as Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub tools.
- Engineers keep access. Goldman has about 12,000 engineers.
- "Strats", staff who mix trading, research and software work, also keep access.

The bank made the change after an internal review of productivity and risk. Staff had used the tools to track client trading, model market moves and make written and visual content.

A Goldman spokesperson, Nick Carcaterra, said the bank gives AI tools to "those who are best suited to leverage them for the long term." The bank's own in-house AI assistant is still widely available, reports say.

This is a change. In July, Goldman's technology chief, Marco Argenti, praised traders and bankers for "vibe coding", which means asking AI to write software in plain language.

## Apple: smaller daily AI budgets

AI tools often charge by "tokens", small pieces of text that the AI reads or writes. Companies pay for every token their staff use.

According to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter:

- In October, Apple cut the daily AI limit for some engineers from $300 to $200. It may lower it to $100 for some teams.
- Many staff outside engineering already have a $100 daily limit. Apple has considered cutting it to as little as $25 for some teams.
- Workers who need more can ask senior leaders for an exception.

Apple staff can use tools including Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini. Apple declined to comment. Some employees said few people came close to the old limit. Others see the cuts as part of a wider push to lower costs under new chief executive John Ternus.

## Why it matters

Many companies rushed to give AI tools to all staff. These moves suggest some are now checking more closely whether the benefits are worth the cost and the risks.

Sources: Bloomberg via FStech, The Star, 9to5Mac, The Next Web

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: Bangladesh agrees to raise garment wages after days of protests
articles.body:
Bangladesh's garment industry wage board agreed on Wednesday, 4 November 2026, to raise the minimum wage for garment workers. The decision followed five days of protests and clashes in the country's main factory areas. The size of the increase has not yet been announced.

## Why it matters

Clothing is the backbone of Bangladesh's economy:

- Bangladesh, with about 170 million people, is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China.
- The sector earns about four-fifths of the country's export income, worth up to $38 billion a year.
- It employs more than four million people and makes clothes for many big international brands.

## What workers want

Workers want the minimum monthly wage raised to 30,000 taka (about $240). The current minimum is 12,500 taka, so their demand would be a 140 percent increase. They say rising prices for food, housing, transport and healthcare have made it hard to live on their pay. Inflation, the rate at which prices rise, is around 8 percent, according to AFP.

## Protests and clashes

Thousands of workers began protesting on Saturday, 31 October. Protesters threw bricks and built barricades, and police fired tear gas.

- On 1 November, clashes in Mirpur, in the capital Dhaka, injured at least 20 people, according to reports.
- On 3 November, reports said a garment worker died in Gazipur, an industrial area near Dhaka, and 10 police officers were hurt in clashes in Dhaka.
- On 4 November, more than 50 people were reported injured and police vehicles were set on fire in Savar, another factory area.

The government set up the wage board on Sunday, 1 November. It includes representatives of both factory owners and workers.

## What happens next

Babul Akter, the workers' representative on the board, said the owners' side also agreed to a raise. "We are working together," he said.

ABM Shamsuddin of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), which represents factory owners, said the board would finish its work by December. That means higher pay could start in January 2027.

Protests continued on Wednesday morning in Gazipur, Mirpur, Narayanganj and Savar while the talks were going on. It is not yet clear whether the promise of a raise will end the unrest, since workers do not yet know how big it will be.

The last major wage rise came in 2023, also after large protests.

Sources: AFP via Free Malaysia Today, Reuters, Al Jazeera, Dhaka Tribune
