articles.title: NASA's Swift space telescope falls back to Earth after 22 years
articles.body:
NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a space telescope that studied the most powerful explosions in the universe, fell back into Earth's atmosphere on Wednesday, 4 November 2026. The US Space Force said it came down at 7:39 a.m. US Eastern time over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia.

NASA expected most of the spacecraft to burn up as it fell, though some parts may have survived.

## What was Swift?

Swift was launched in 2004 and named after Neil Gehrels, an American astronomer who led the mission. It was built to study gamma-ray bursts. These are short, extremely bright flashes of high-energy light, often caused when huge stars collapse or when dead stars crash into each other.

Swift was planned to work for only two years, but it kept going for almost 22. Its strengths were:

- Three telescopes that together covered a wide range of light.
- The ability to turn quickly and point at short-lived events in the sky.
- Sending fast alerts to other observatories around the world, so they could study the same events.

Over its life, Swift helped scientists learn about black holes at the centres of galaxies, stars that give off X-ray flares, exploding stars called supernovae, and comets and asteroids in our own solar system.

## Why did it fall?

All satellites in low orbit slowly lose height because of drag, the slowing force from the very thin air at that altitude. When the Sun is very active, it heats the upper atmosphere and makes it expand, which increases this drag. NASA said recent solar activity made Swift sink quickly.

A fast, high-risk servicing mission was planned to boost the telescope to a higher orbit. But NASA said it ended in August without attempting the boost. After that, drag increased again.

On 20 October, Swift reached a height of 275 kilometres (171 miles). It could no longer make up for the drag and went into safe mode, a protective state where it stops normal work. The team at Penn State University, which ran the mission, then sent a command that effectively ended its operations. Its last gamma-ray burst detection came on 17 October.

## Its legacy

NASA described Swift's records as "a treasure trove of science observations." Even with the telescope gone, scientists around the world will keep using its data for years.

Sources: NASA, ScienceDaily, BBC Sky at Night Magazine

articles.title: AI deepfakes hit US midterm races, including Russian-linked fake video
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
AI-made fake videos, called deepfakes, appeared in several races in the US midterm elections, which ended on 3 November 2026. The most serious case was a fake video about a Texas Senate candidate that researchers linked to a Russian influence network.

## The Texas case

On 20 October, one day after early voting began in Texas, a new account on X posted two videos. In them, a young man claimed to be a former student of James Talarico, the Democratic Senate candidate, and accused him of abuse in 2012.

The claim was false. Private researchers acted within 24 hours:

- Graphika, a research firm, linked the accounts that spread the video to Storm-1516, a known Russian influence network.
- NewsGuard, which tracks false information, said the video was made with AI.
- AFP fact-checkers found the account had copied the Facebook page of a real former student.
- The real former student told fact-checkers that the man in the videos was not him and that Talarico never abused him.

X suspended the account. The US government had not publicly named who was behind it, according to a 26 October analysis by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), a Washington research group.

## AI search tools repeated the claim

NewsGuard found that Google's AI Overview, the AI summary shown above search results, repeated the accusation. It cited news articles that never mentioned it. Google's Gemini and Microsoft's Copilot chatbots also presented the claim as real until fact-checks were published. This shows how AI tools can spread false stories quickly.

Talarico went on to win the race, according to Time magazine.

## Other deepfakes

Time reported other cases:

- In Maine, deepfake videos appeared to show Troy Jackson threatening campaign staff the week before the vote. He still won by more than seven points.
- In Wisconsin, Republican Derrick Van Orden posted deepfake videos of his opponent, Rebecca Cooke, saying things she never said. He lost.

Time concluded that deepfakes did not appear to have a very large effect on results in many races. Some campaigns now face legal threats over AI-made ads, Axios reported.

## What comes next

Experts quoted by Time expect new state and federal AI bills. Many voters also told pollsters that AI and data centres were important issues in this election.

Sources: Foundation for Defense of Democracies, Time, NewsGuard, Axios

articles.title: Saudi Arabia and Syria Sign a Defence Deal and $403 Million in Loans
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
On November 4, 2026, Saudi Arabia and Syria signed a defence cooperation agreement and several other deals in Riyadh. Saudi Arabia also agreed to lend Syria more than $403 million for rebuilding.

The deals were signed during a visit by Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, who met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. It was al-Sharaa's second visit to Riyadh in less than a month. The two leaders also met there on October 6.

## The defence agreement

The agreement was signed by the defence ministries of both countries. Syria's Foreign Ministry called it the "most notable" deal of the visit. However, neither government has made its details public, so it is not known what it includes.

Reuters reported in October that Syria was considering giving military help to Saudi Arabia against Houthi missile and drone attacks. A Syrian diplomat said any such help would go through official agreements. It is not confirmed whether the new deal covers this.

## The loans

The Saudi Fund for Development signed six loan agreements with Syria's Finance Ministry. They are "concessional" loans, which means they have easier terms than normal bank loans. Al Jazeera listed these uses:

- $100 million to rebuild and equip damaged health facilities
- $105 million for civil defence (emergency and rescue services)
- $90 million to repair the Aleppo thermal power plant
- $60 million to repair damaged homes
- $30 million for drinking water systems in Damascus and Idlib

These five items add up to $385 million. Reports did not explain the remaining amount.

The two countries also signed agreements on industry, agriculture and protecting the environment.

## What the leaders said

The two leaders talked about rising tension in the region, safe shipping and energy supplies. They called for an immediate end to actions that threaten ships in the Red Sea, the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the Strait of Hormuz.

## Background

Al-Sharaa came to power after President Bashar al-Assad was removed in December 2024. Since then, Saudi Arabia has been one of the strongest supporters of Syria's new government.

Days before the visit, Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said at the Manama Dialogue, a security meeting in Bahrain, that talks were under way about Syria joining the "Mecca alliance", a defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan. In the same week, Saudi airline flyadeal launched direct flights between Madinah and Damascus, according to Arab News.

Sources: Al Jazeera, Reuters, Saudi Press Agency, Enab Baladi, Arab News

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: Saudi Aramco Takes 49% of the Kingdom’s AI Company HUMAIN
articles.body:
Saudi Aramco, the giant state oil company, now owns 49% of HUMAIN, Saudi Arabia's national AI company. The deal closed on 1 November 2026, and Aramco gave details when it reported its third-quarter results on 4 November.

## The deal

- Aramco pays with some of its own AI assets plus about 9.9 billion Saudi riyals (about $2.6 billion) in cash.
- The Public Investment Fund (PIF), Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, keeps the other 51%.
- The two sides first agreed on non-binding terms in October 2025.
- The companies have not said exactly which AI assets Aramco is putting into HUMAIN.

## What HUMAIN does

HUMAIN was launched in May 2025. It builds data centres, cloud computing services and AI models, including ALLaM, an AI model for the Arabic language. Its chief executive, Tareq Amin, used to lead Aramco Digital, the oil company's technology unit.

HUMAIN plans to build 3 gigawatts of AI data-centre capacity by 2030. A gigawatt is a very large amount of electricity, roughly what a big power station produces. The company also wants to become one of the world's leading exporters of AI services. Earlier reports describe partnerships with Amazon Web Services, Saudi Telecom Company and Elon Musk's xAI.

## Why Aramco is involved

Aramco says it will use HUMAIN's computing power to bring AI into its oil and industrial operations. It also expects to earn more from the AI and digital assets it already owns. Aramco's chief executive, Amin Nasser, said the company has gained $11.3 billion in "Technology Realized Value" since 2023, with a large part coming from AI.

PIF's Yazeed Al-Humied said that bringing the AI businesses together under HUMAIN will help grow talent, technology and intellectual property.

The two organisations are already closely linked: PIF owns 16% of Aramco, and PIF governor Yasir Al Rumayyan is Aramco's chairman.

## Aramco's results

Aramco reported adjusted net income of $31.2 billion for the third quarter, up from $28.6 billion a year earlier.

## The wider Gulf picture

The deal is part of a strong push by Gulf states to become AI centres, using their energy and money to build data centres. In neighbouring Abu Dhabi in the UAE, the national oil company ADNOC has signed a deal with OpenAI and the local AI company G42. Some reports, including from Semafor, say Saudi Arabia is now looking more to companies such as Aramco and outside investors to pay for its AI plans.

Sources: The Next Web, Semafor, Data Center Dynamics

articles.title: Saudi economy shrinks 3.8% as the war cuts oil output
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia's economy shrank by 3.8% in the third quarter of 2026 (July to September), compared with the same months last year. The early figures came from the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT) on 1 November. Two days later, the Finance Ministry reported a large budget deficit for the same quarter.

## Oil falls, other business grows a little

GDP (gross domestic product) is the total value of everything a country produces. It was the second quarter in a row in which the Saudi economy got smaller. In the second quarter it fell by 4.7%.

- Oil activity fell by 20.4% compared with a year earlier. In the second quarter it had fallen by 24.8%.
- Non-oil activity, such as trade, building and services, grew by 1.9%, up from 0.8% in the second quarter.
- Government activity fell by 2.7%.

Compared with the second quarter, the economy grew by 1.3%, as oil activity picked up again. GASTAT says these are early estimates and may change.

## Why oil fell

Reports link the fall to the war that began after US and Israeli strikes on Iran on 28 February 2026. The war has badly limited shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea route used by much of the Gulf's oil. Saudi Arabia has sent more oil by pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu instead. But reports say attacks in September forced that pipeline to stop for a time.

The Houthi missile and drone attacks on Riyadh in October are not part of these figures.

## A bigger budget gap

On 3 November the Finance Ministry reported a deficit of 84 billion riyals (about $22.4 billion) for the third quarter. A deficit means the government spent more than it earned. Reports say oil income fell by almost 40% from the second quarter.

The government expects the economy to shrink by 3.6% in 2026 and a deficit of 4.9% of GDP. Some economists expect a larger deficit, near 5.6% to 6%. The government says it will keep borrowing to cover the gap.

The IMF (International Monetary Fund) expects the Saudi economy to shrink by 3.3% this year and then grow by 7.9% in 2027. It says Saudi savings and its other oil export routes are softening the damage, and that the kingdom is in a better position than several Gulf neighbours. Reports say Saudi crude exports have since recovered to their highest level of the war.

Sources: Arab News, General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT), Investing.com, Bloomberg via Briefs Finance

articles.title: Nvidia tells cloud partners to limit business with Chinese customers, FT says
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Nvidia, the company that makes most of the chips used to train AI, has told its data centre partners to limit how much they sell to Chinese customers. The Financial Times (FT) reported this on 3 November 2026, citing five people who know about the matter.

## The 51% rule

A data centre is a large building full of computers. Many companies rent computing power from cloud providers that run these centres, often using Nvidia chips.

According to the FT:

- Nvidia told cloud and data centre partners that at least 51% of their services must be sold to non-Chinese companies.
- The rule covers only new contracts. Existing deals are not affected.
- Nvidia gave the message by word of mouth, through its sales and regional teams, not in writing.
- Nvidia had not set this kind of limit before.

Some reports say the rule applies around the world. It is not clear how the 51% will be measured or checked.

## What Nvidia and China said

Nvidia did not confirm or deny the report. In a statement, it said: "America cannot win the AI race unless America's AI infrastructure wins worldwide." It said US policy encourages cloud providers to build on American technology.

Mao Ning, a spokeswoman for China's foreign ministry, said she did not know about the report. She said China hopes all sides will offer a "fair, transparent and non-discriminatory" business environment for companies from every country.

## Why it matters

The US has blocked sales of Nvidia's most advanced chips to China since 2022. But many Chinese AI companies rent computing power from cloud providers outside China to train their AI models. The US has tried for years to close this route. Reports say countries such as Singapore and Malaysia host some of this rented capacity.

Some chips also reach China through smuggling. Earlier this year, several senior staff at the server maker Super Micro were charged with smuggling about $2.5 billion worth of Nvidia AI servers into China.

A Singapore-based cloud provider told reporters it is hard to find enough non-Chinese customers outside the US, and that strict enforcement would hurt its business.

Nvidia is the world's most valuable company. Its rules for partners can shape where AI is built and who can use it.

Sources: Financial Times via The Next Web, AFP, The Standard (Hong Kong)

articles.title: Turkey's inflation stays near 30% as prices jump in October
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Annual inflation in Turkey rose slightly to 29.77% in October 2026, from 29.73% in September. The Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat), the official statistics office, published the figures on November 3.

Inflation is the rate at which prices go up. An annual rate of 29.77% means that, on average, prices were almost 30% higher than in October 2025.

## Bigger monthly rise

The yearly rate barely moved, but prices rose fast during the month itself.

- Prices rose 2.58% in October alone, up from 1.84% in September. This was the biggest monthly rise in six months.
- Prices have risen 27.52% since the start of 2026.
- Economists had expected annual inflation of about 29.56%, so the result was a little higher than forecast.

Core inflation, which leaves out prices that move a lot, such as energy, unprocessed food, tobacco and gold, was 28.46% a year.

## What got more expensive

The biggest yearly rises were in:

- Housing, water, electricity, gas and fuel: up 40.24%.
- Transport: up 36.39%.
- Food and non-alcoholic drinks: up 27.73%.

Food added the most to the overall rate, followed by transport and housing. In October alone, food prices rose 3.50%.

Producer prices, which measure what factories and businesses receive for their goods, rose 27.41% from a year earlier, according to Trading Economics.

## Different measures

Some Turkish economists do not trust the official figures. An independent group called ENAG, made up of academics, said annual inflation was 45.12% in October, down from 46.61% in September. ENAG's numbers are not official, and its methods differ from TurkStat's.

## Interest rates

The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey cut its main interest rate by 1 percentage point to 36% in October. Central banks use high interest rates to slow price rises. Qatar News Agency noted that the latest rise in monthly prices has increased attention on whether the bank will cut rates again before the end of the year.

Turkey has had high inflation for several years. In October 2025, annual inflation was 32.87%, so the rate has come down over the past year, but slowly.

Sources: Qatar News Agency, TurkStat, Trading Economics, Azernews

articles.title: Google turns off AI for school students by default, sparking a Search row
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Google said on 3 November 2026 that it will switch off its AI products by default for school students who use its education software. But schools that say no to the AI will also lose Google Search by default, which caused strong criticism.

## What Google changed

Until now, Google's Gemini AI tools were turned on automatically for schools using Google Classroom. Under the new setup, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search are 'entirely off' for student accounts from kindergarten to grade 12, until school administrators turn them on.

Chris Phillips, Google's vice president for education, wrote that 'schools should have control over AI in their classrooms.'

After the backlash, Google said schools can turn on Search alone, without the Gemini products. However, Search still includes AI features such as AI-written summaries, so schools cannot use Search without any AI. Google said the change gives 'schools more choice, not less'. It also said its AI tools will try to guide students step by step instead of simply giving answers to homework.

## Criticism

- Randi Weingarten, head of the American Federation of Teachers, a large teachers' union, said Google 'prioritized its business interests over the education of our children.'
- Josh Golin of Fairplay, a children's advocacy group, said Google was pressuring schools to use its AI.
- Earlier, in October, 13 parent groups had urged school districts to turn off Gemini and YouTube.

Google has a very large role in US schools. Most Chromebook laptops are bought by school districts for students. Researchers at Stanford say there are still no high-quality studies showing how student use of AI affects learning.

## New York City's ban list

Cities and states are also writing their own rules. In New York City, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced limits on student-facing AI tools just before the school year began. On 23 October, the news site Chalkbeat published the city's list of 38 education products that were blocked or had AI features disabled.

- Amira, an AI reading tutor used in more than 200 schools, was banned outright.
- The city's own AI chatbot, built with Microsoft, was switched off for students.
- Some companies said they do not use the kind of AI the policy targets and asked to be removed from the list.

Officials are working with companies case by case. Some firms turned off their AI features and were allowed back.

Sources: NBC News, Chalkbeat, EdSource

articles.title: Asian Cup 2027 in Saudi Arabia Moved to December Over Security Fears
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
On November 3, 2026, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it would delay the 2027 AFC Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia by almost a year. The tournament will now start in December 2027 instead of January 2027. The decision follows months of Houthi missile and drone attacks on the kingdom.

The Asian Cup is the biggest football tournament for national teams in Asia. The 2027 edition will have 24 teams.

## The new dates

- Old dates: January 7 to February 5, 2027, with the opening match in Riyadh
- New dates: December 23, 2027 to January 21, 2028

The AFC will send the new dates to FIFA, world football's governing body, for approval.

## Why it was moved

The AFC said it made the decision "in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region". It mentioned difficult logistics and travel problems. It said the change was "in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders."

The AFC decided after talks with the local organising committee and the Saudi Arabian Football Federation. Reports said the AFC had faced growing pressure from Asian football associations worried about the safety of players and fans. Only about a week earlier, the AFC had said the tournament would go ahead as planned. Yasser Al-Misehal, head of the local organising committee, said Saudi Arabia had been fully ready to host on the original dates.

The Houthis, an Iran-backed armed group in Yemen, have attacked Saudi airports, oil sites and cities since a truce in Yemen collapsed in July 2026. A strike on Riyadh's main airport on October 10 killed at least 12 people.

## Other events affected

Several other international events in Saudi Arabia have been moved, delayed or cancelled. According to The National and Al-Monitor:

- Golf: the Asian Tour postponed the Saudi International with no new date.
- Cycling: the Urban World Championships were cancelled.
- Rally: the World Rally Championship's final round moved to Italy in September, and the 2027 Dakar Rally was moved out of Saudi Arabia.
- Tennis: the WTA Finals moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells in the United States. The Six Kings Slam exhibition in Riyadh, with Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic, was moved from October to December.
- Football: an AFC Champions League Elite match between Al Nassr and Al Wasl in Riyadh was postponed in October. Some domestic matches were also affected.

Saudi Arabia has invested heavily in sport as part of Vision 2030, its plan to grow the economy beyond oil. It is also preparing to host the FIFA World Cup in 2034.

Sources: Al Jazeera, Reuters, The National, Al-Monitor, Khaleej Times

articles.title: Oman's economy grows 5.1% as oil output rises, IMF sees about 4% this year
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Oman's economy grew by 5.1% in the second quarter of 2026, compared with the same period last year, according to early official data published in October. In early November, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said it expects Oman to grow by about 4% over the whole of 2026.

## Oil leads the growth

The figures come from Oman's National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI). They are preliminary, which means they may still change. They compare April to June 2026 with April to June 2025, using constant prices to remove the effect of inflation.

- Total GDP: about 9.9 billion Omani rials, up 5.1%.
- Oil-related activities: about 3.4 billion rials, up 14.7%.
- Non-oil activities: about 7 billion rials, up only 0.7%.
- Services: up 1.5%.
- Agriculture and fishing: up 2.3%.
- Industry: down 1.5%.

So most of the growth came from oil. The non-oil part of the economy, which the government wants to expand, grew much more slowly. An October brief from Oman's Ministry of Economy stressed the need to keep non-oil sectors growing.

## What the IMF says

The Oman Observer reported the IMF view on November 2, after a meeting in Muscat. Dr Abdullah al Hassan, who leads the IMF team for Oman, said the outlook had not changed much from last year, but the risks had increased. This comes during a year of war and tension in the region.

The IMF's main points, as reported:

- Growth of about 4% in 2026 and about 3% a year on average in the medium term.
- Inflation of about 3% this year.
- Government budget surpluses of about 5% of GDP this year and next. A surplus means the government earns more than it spends.
- The current account, which measures money flowing in and out of the country through trade and income, should return to surplus in 2026 after a deficit last year.
- Oman aims to raise oil production capacity to 1.2 million barrels per day.

Other forecasters are a little more careful. Standard Chartered bank expects growth of 3.5% in both 2026 and 2027.

## Longer-term plans

Oman's long-term economic plan is called Oman Vision 2040. Like Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, it aims to make the country less dependent on oil and gas. In late October, Oman offered new areas for mining companies and started the second phase of its Digital Economy Programme, according to official reports.

Sources: Oman Observer, NCSI, WAM, Entrepreneur Middle East

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: Anthropic Files to Go Public, Showing Fast Growth and Huge Computing Costs
articles.body:
Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude AI models, has filed papers to sell its shares to the public. It published its filing with the US markets regulator, the SEC, on 26 October 2026, and added new figures on 2 November.

A company that "goes public" lets anyone buy its shares on a stock exchange. Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq exchange under the short name "ANT". No date and no share price had been set when the papers were published.

## What the numbers show

The filing gives the public its first detailed look at the company's money. According to CNBC and Fortune:

- Revenue (money from sales) was $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with $1.16 billion a year earlier.
- Revenue in the third quarter (July to September) was about $17 billion.
- Growth from one quarter to the next slowed to about 47%, down from about 144% in the second quarter.
- The company made an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter, after a $974 million operating profit in the second quarter.
- About 80% of first-half revenue came from customers who pay for how much they use, and the rest came from subscriptions.

Anthropic said the third-quarter loss came mainly from computing power it bought on short-term deals. The filing says this short-term computing "currently costs significantly more" than computing bought under its long-term contracts.

## Very large computing commitments

AI companies need huge numbers of chips in data centres to train and run their models. The updated filing says Anthropic has agreed to spend about $895.4 billion on purchases and leases, almost all of it for computing and infrastructure. Partners named in the first filing include Amazon, Google, Microsoft, AMD and SpaceX.

## Risks and control

The risk section of the filing is more than 90 pages long. It lists dangers such as a dispute with the US government over a Pentagon "supply chain risk" label, dependence on chips made by TSMC in Taiwan, local opposition to data centres, and the risk that AI models could be misused.

The founders will keep 50.1% of the voting power through a special company, so they will keep control after the listing. Amazon will hold shares without votes. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the sale.

The company's last private funding round, in May, valued it at $965 billion. Some analysts quoted in the press expect a higher value at listing, but this is only an estimate until the share price is set.

Sources: CNBC, Fortune, US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)

articles.title: BYD sells a record number of electric cars in October as China's EV race heats up
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
China's BYD, the world's biggest maker of electric cars, sold a record number of fully electric cars in October 2026. According to Electrek, the company sold 305,743 battery-electric cars in the month. That is 37% more than a year earlier, and the first time BYD passed 300,000 in one month.

## The numbers

BYD sells two main types of "new energy vehicles": battery-electric cars (BEVs), which run only on electricity, and plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), which have both a battery and a petrol engine. Electrek reported these October figures:

- Total new energy vehicles: 490,168, up 11% from October 2025
- Battery-electric cars: 305,743, up 37%
- Plug-in hybrids: 177,382, down 17%
- Cars sold outside China: 170,194

Different reports use slightly different totals, depending on which vehicles they count. The trend is the same: BYD is selling more fully electric cars and fewer hybrids.

BYD has sold more than 1.5 million cars abroad so far in 2026, nearly double last year. It is growing in Europe, Southeast Asia and Latin America. Electrek says BYD expects about 2 million overseas sales in 2026. BYD is also promoting new models with its "Blade Battery 2.0" and fast charging.

## Strong competition in China

Other Chinese carmakers also grew quickly, according to CarNewsChina:

- Leapmotor sold 106,127 cars, up about 51%
- Xpeng sold a record 50,237 cars, up about 20%
- Geely sold 214,996 new energy vehicles

Not every company did well. Sales by Huawei's car partners (HIMA) fell by about half compared with a year earlier, and Li Auto's sales also fell.

## Weak sales in the United States

The US market is moving the other way. Kelley Blue Book estimates Americans bought about 262,600 new electric cars in the third quarter of 2026, almost 40% fewer than a year before. This means BYD's fully electric sales in one month were higher than all US electric car sales in three months.

Tesla's sales of China-made cars fell about 10% in October to 61,497, according to reports. In Australia, battery-electric cars outsold petrol-only cars for the third month in a row in October.

Sources: Electrek, CarNewsChina, Kelley Blue Book, Stocktwits

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: India's opposition rallies in Delhi for election chief to resign
articles.body:
Tens of thousands of opposition supporters rallied in New Delhi on Sunday, 1 November 2026, demanding that India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, resign. They accuse the Election Commission of removing huge numbers of voters from the lists in a way that helps the ruling party.

The rally at Ramlila Maidan, a large ground in the capital, was led by Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress party and Leader of the Opposition in the lower house of parliament. It was the biggest event so far in protests that began in late September.

## What is the dispute?

The Election Commission is the body that runs elections in India, the world's largest democracy. It has carried out a big review of voter lists, known as the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR.

- Media reports say more than 133 million names were removed from the lists.
- Critics say minorities, especially Muslims, were hit hardest.
- The protests grew after Indian media reported that two deputy election commissioners had raised formal concerns about voter registration systems and the list changes.

The Election Commission denies any wrongdoing. It says the review removed duplicate entries, dead people and fraudulent registrations, and that anyone wrongly removed can register again. In a 26 October filing to the Supreme Court, it said all orders on the review were issued with the agreement of all three commission members.

The ruling BJP party, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, called the opposition's claims "completely misleading."

## Weeks of protests

The 1 November rally followed weeks of marches:

- On 12 October, thousands marched towards the Supreme Court. Authorities closed several metro stations and deployed thousands of police.
- Police detained thousands of protesters over that weekend. Reporters Without Borders said at least 16 journalists were detained while covering the protests.
- Gandhi has filed a petition with the Supreme Court against the Election Commission on behalf of opposition leaders.
- A youth group has held almost daily protests and says it will continue until Kumar steps down.

At the Delhi rally, Gandhi spoke from an open-top vehicle. He said removing the election chief was the first step to protect democracy and that people were "not prepared to accept" the voter removals.

Home Minister Amit Shah criticised the choice of date, saying it hurt victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, which began on 1 November that year.

## What next

As of early November, Kumar has not resigned and there is no sign that he plans to. The case before the Supreme Court is likely to be the next key moment.

Sources: Al Jazeera, Daily Times, AFP, France 24

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: Kimi Antonelli, 20, becomes youngest Formula 1 world champion
articles.body:
Italian driver Kimi Antonelli won the Formula 1 world championship on Sunday, 1 November 2026, at the age of 20. He became the youngest champion in the history of the sport after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Formula 1 (F1) is the top level of international motor racing. Its season includes more than 20 races around the world, and the driver with the most points at the end wins the title.

## The race and the record

Antonelli only needed to finish ninth or better in Mexico City to be sure of the title. Max Verstappen of Red Bull won the race, Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari came second and Antonelli finished third. He clinched the championship with four races of the season still to go.

- Reports put his age at 20 years and 68 days.
- He beat the record of Germany's Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 years and 134 days old when he won in 2010.
- He is the 36th different F1 world champion.
- He ends Italy's 73-year wait for a third world champion driver.

## A fast rise

This was only Antonelli's second season in F1. He drives for Mercedes, and in 2025 he took the seat left by Lewis Hamilton, who moved to Ferrari. He is the first driver from the Mercedes junior programme, which trains young racers, to win the title.

His teammate George Russell started 2026 as the favourite and won the first race in Australia. But Antonelli soon took over:

- He won five races in a row, starting at the Chinese Grand Prix.
- He became the youngest championship leader in F1 history after winning in Japan, aged 19.
- He also won in Belgium and Spain, and in Italy, where he won his home race at Monza after starting 19th. He was the first Italian to win at home since 1966.

## Reactions

Antonelli called it "a day I will remember forever." Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff described him as a "role model for modern F1." Rival drivers praised his season as "close to perfection."

Russell, whose own title hopes faded, said the season "will not break me."

The remaining four races will decide the other places in the drivers' standings and the constructors' championship.

Sources: ESPN, Formula1.com, Motorsport.com, Sky Sports

articles.title: OPEC+ Holds Oil Output Steady as War Pushes Prices Past $110
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
On November 1, 2026, seven oil-producing countries in the OPEC+ group, led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, decided not to raise oil production in December. It was the third month in a row without an increase.

OPEC+ is a group of oil exporters. It includes OPEC (the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) and partners such as Russia. A smaller group of seven members now meets every month to set production levels: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman.

## The decision

At an online meeting, the seven countries agreed to keep December production at the same level as September 2026. They said they had reviewed "global market conditions and outlook". Their next meeting is on November 29, 2026.

Earlier in 2026, the group raised production every month. Reports say it added 188,000 barrels per day each month from June to September, a total of 752,000 barrels per day. It then paused in October, November and now December.

At the October 4 meeting, the combined target for the seven countries was set at 31.01 million barrels per day. Saudi Arabia's share was 10.478 million barrels per day, the largest. These numbers are targets. Reports say real supply has been lower, because some members cannot produce more and others must make up for producing too much before.

## Prices driven by war

Oil prices have stayed high because of conflicts in the region.

- On September 25, after the Houthis of Yemen claimed attacks on Aramco sites in Yanbu and on Riyadh, Brent crude (the main world oil price) closed above $106.50 a barrel.
- On October 22, Brent rose 4% to $113.17 a barrel, its highest close since May. That day, Reuters reported that Aramco told staff to leave its Dhahran headquarters.

Morgan Stanley, a US bank, estimated that Middle East crude exports were about 17 million barrels per day in one October week. The data firm Kpler put the average at about 18 million barrels per day in the 12 months before the Iran war. The war between the US, Israel and Iran began in February 2026 and has disrupted shipping from the Gulf.

An analyst at Sparta Commodities told Al Jazeera that oil would likely stay above $100 while the war on Iran continues.

## What it means

High prices bring more money per barrel, but Gulf producers are also facing attacks and transport problems. Saudi Arabia's finance ministry expects oil activity in the kingdom to fall by 21.8% in 2026. We could not find a confirmed oil price for early November.

Sources: OPEC, Reuters, Al Jazeera, Nairametrics, Nation Thailand

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: Ransomware attacks on hospitals hit 2026 high in October
articles.body:
Hospitals and other health providers faced more ransomware attacks in October 2026 than in any other month this year, according to a monthly count by the research firm Comparitech. In total, the firm recorded 1,020 ransomware attacks around the world in October.

## What is ransomware?

Ransomware is a type of cyberattack. Criminals break into computer systems, lock files or steal data, and then demand money, called a ransom, to unlock the systems or not publish the data. Attacks on hospitals can delay treatment and force staff to use paper records.

## The numbers for October

- 1,020 attacks in total, about 33 per day. This was the second-highest monthly total of 2026, after August (1,034).
- 85 attacks on healthcare providers, the highest monthly figure of the year.
- 47 attacks on schools and universities, also a new high for the year.
- 42 attacks on government bodies.
- 61 attacks on transport companies, more than double the figure for August and September.

Most of these attacks are claims made by criminal gangs on their own websites. Only 81 were confirmed by the organisations that were hit. The United States had the most attacks, followed by Germany and Spain.

## Examples from health and government

Comparitech listed incidents including:

- Kamalnayan Bajaj Hospital in India, claimed by a group called Crypto24.
- UNM Health in the US state of New Mexico, which did not pay a ransom.
- AMSAM, a health organisation in France.
- Croatia's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, where a group offered stolen data for sale.
- Towns in Germany and Sweden that said they paid no ransom.

In Japan, an attack on data centre company IDC Frontier affected about 500 companies and local authorities. In Denmark, an attack on a contractor delayed work on the Fehmarnbelt tunnel, a road and rail tunnel being built between Denmark and Germany.

## The most active gangs

The most active groups in October were The Gentlemen, with 139 claimed attacks, and Qilin, with 125. A group called N0n claimed 85 attacks, up from 17 in September.

## Staying safe

Security experts often advise organisations to keep software updated, use strong passwords with a second login check, and keep offline backups so that systems can be restored without paying criminals.

Sources: Comparitech

articles.title: Gaza Ceasefire One Year On: Hostages Freed, but Most Promises Unfulfilled
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
On October 10, 2026, the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas in Gaza reached its first anniversary. The truce is still formally in place, but Israeli strikes continue almost every day, and the main parts of the peace plan have not happened.

Hamas is the Palestinian armed group that ruled Gaza and led the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel. The ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, under a plan backed by US President Donald Trump.

## What has been achieved

- Three days after the deal, Hamas freed the last 20 living hostages taken on October 7, 2023.
- Israel reports one full year without Hamas rocket fire from Gaza.
- The US military and its partners set up a command post near Gaza to watch the truce.

## What has not happened

Hamas has not given up its weapons. In July 2026, Hamas chose Khalil al-Hayya as its leader and said it would disarm. Trump called this a breakthrough. But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu demands proof that all weapons are handed over, "down to individual guns", and Israel has not begun to withdraw its forces.

Under the deal, Israeli forces could stay in 53% of Gaza. According to official accounts reported by AFP, they now control about 70%.

A Palestinian technocratic body (a group of experts, not politicians), the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, is led by Ali Shaath. Hamas said in July it would hand control to this committee. But AFP reports that Hamas still controls security in practice.

An International Stabilization Force was planned to protect aid deliveries and train Palestinian police. Several countries pledged troops, but many said they would deploy only after Hamas disarmament is clearly agreed.

## Rebuilding and money

Trump set up a "Board of Peace" to oversee Gaza's recovery, with former British Prime Minister Tony Blair as a key figure. Trump promised $10 billion of US money in January, and Gulf countries pledged more. AFP reports that no money is known to have reached Gaza's reconstruction yet. In September 2026, the board proposed a $2.45 billion, six-month recovery plan.

## The human cost

Gaza's Health Ministry said that as of late October 2026, Israeli attacks since the ceasefire had killed 1,574 Palestinians and wounded 5,687. The UN considers the ministry's figures reliable. On October 31, medical sources reported two more deaths. In total, the ministry says more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed since October 2023, and around 90% of civilian infrastructure has been destroyed.

Sources: AFP, Oman Observer, Anadolu Agency, Express Tribune, Associated Press, Al Jazeera

articles.title: Riyadh Season opens, but several big Saudi events move to later dates
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Riyadh Season, Saudi Arabia's biggest yearly entertainment festival, opened on October 21, 2026. Its main zone, Boulevard World, opened on October 30. But several other big events in the kingdom this autumn have been moved to later dates.

## Riyadh Season 2026

This is the seventh Riyadh Season. It is run under the General Entertainment Authority (GEA), the government body for the entertainment sector. GEA chairman Turki Alalshikh announced the dates in September.

- Theme: "Big Time".
- A main programme of about ten weeks, with boxing, wrestling, UFC fights, concerts, theatre, comedy and family shows.
- Zones include Boulevard World, Boulevard City, Wonder Garden, The Groves and the Farmers' Market.
- Visit Saudi lists the season as running until March 1, 2027. Boulevard World stays open until May 22, 2027.

Boulevard World has areas styled on different countries and cultures. The Saudi Press Agency said tickets were sold through the webook platform.

## Six Kings Slam moved to December

On October 14, Riyadh Season said the Six Kings Slam would move from October 21 to 24 to December 27 to 30, 2026. It will still be held in Riyadh.

The Six Kings Slam is an exhibition tennis event. It gives no ranking points but offers very large prize money. Italy's Jannik Sinner won the first two editions, beating Carlos Alcaraz in both finals.

Organisers cited "organisational and logistical challenges". Some reports linked the move to recent Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, but organisers did not make that link. Tennis news reports noted that the new dates end just 48 hours before the 2027 season begins in Australia, and it is not yet confirmed that all six players can attend.

## Other changes

- Red Sea International Film Festival: On September 21, the Red Sea Film Foundation postponed the sixth festival, planned for December 3 to 12 in Jeddah, to late 2027. It cited timing and logistics. Year-round film activities continue, including events at Culture Square in Historic Jeddah from November.
- MDLBEAST Soundstorm: The music festival, planned for December 3 and 4 in Riyadh, will not go ahead as planned. Organisers told ticket holders it "will be postponed". Some outlets called it cancelled for 2026, and no new date has been confirmed.
- Future Investment Initiative: The big investment conference planned for late October was moved to 2027.

Saudi Arabia uses events like these to grow tourism, a key part of Vision 2030, its plan to rely less on oil.

Sources: Gulf News, Arab News, The National, Saudi Press Agency, Tennis Majors, DJ Mag

articles.title: OpenAI cuts funding round target by $10 billion as tech shares fall
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, has lowered the target for its newest funding round by $10 billion. The Financial Times reported the news on 30 October 2026, and Reuters repeated it, citing people who know about the matter.

## What changed

A funding round is when a private company sells part of itself to investors to raise money. According to the reports, OpenAI is now looking for about $20 billion. The value it hoped to be given has also dropped:

- The target valuation fell to $1.25 trillion, down from $1.4 trillion.
- Investors had until Friday, 30 October, to promise their money.
- The first part of the round, called the 'first close', is expected to raise less than $20 billion, because some investors chose to put in less money than planned.

Later, wealthy individuals will be able to invest through a separate offer at the same $1.25 trillion valuation, the reports said.

## Who is investing

The biggest investor is expected to be a group from the United Arab Emirates that includes MGX, a state-backed technology investment fund in Abu Dhabi. In return, OpenAI would get the option to rent new computing capacity being built in the region.

Well-known US venture capital firms are also expected to take part. These include Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz. OpenAI, MGX and several of the firms did not answer Reuters' requests for comment.

## Why it happened

The cut came during a sharp fall in US technology shares. Many investors are worried about how much money companies are spending on AI. The Nasdaq, a US stock index full of tech companies, fell 2.9% on 30 October. It was 7.8% below its record closing level from 6 October.

OpenAI plans to list its shares on a stock market in 2027. Reuters reported that OpenAI wanted to finish this round partly before rival Anthropic lists its own shares, because both companies are asking a similar group of investors for money.

## Revenue is still growing

The news does not mean OpenAI's business is shrinking. Earlier in October, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI expects its annualised revenue to reach at least $70 billion by the end of 2026. Annualised revenue means the amount it would earn in a year at its current pace. At the end of September, that figure was about $50 billion, according to Bloomberg's sources.

OpenAI has not publicly confirmed the new funding numbers.

Sources: Financial Times (via Reuters), Reuters, Bloomberg

articles.title: Norway court blocks Meta terms that publishers said allowed AI scraping
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
A court in Oslo, Norway, on 28 October 2026 temporarily blocked new business terms from Meta, the owner of Facebook and Instagram. News publishers said the terms would let Meta copy their articles for its AI products.

## What the terms said

Meta's updated terms would give it broad rights to collect, or 'scrape', content from publishers that use Facebook or Instagram, even content published only on their own websites. The Norwegian publishers' group MBL said 'every single article, every picture and every video, even those behind paywalls, can be scraped.' A paywall is a barrier that only lets paying readers see content.

Meta had removed a direct mention of AI training. But publishers said the new wording, about improving 'advertising and business products', still covered its AI services.

## The court case

On 27 October, MBL asked the Oslo District Court to stop the terms. Its members include Schibsted, Amedia, NRK and TV2. The next day, the court ruled that a court must first review whether the terms are legal before they can take effect. Norway's public broadcaster NRK reported that Meta must pay about 1 million Norwegian kroner in costs.

Meta spokesperson Andy Stone said Meta will hold a full consultation with publishers, and that the old terms stay in place until it ends. Reports say the changes, planned for 20 November, are now paused.

## Reaction in other countries

- UK: the Competition and Markets Authority, the competition regulator, opened an investigation on 30 October into whether the terms are unfair to publishers and advertisers, the Copyright Alliance reported.
- Denmark and Sweden: publisher groups complained to competition authorities.
- Canada: News Media Canada called the terms 'a unilateral act of aggression against publishers.'
- US: Senators Adam Schiff and Marsha Blackburn wrote to Meta objecting to the terms.

## A busy month for AI copyright cases

October also saw many new lawsuits about AI and copyright. Copyright means the legal right of creators to control how their work is used. The Copyright Alliance listed several cases:

- 6 October: Canadian news groups, including The Globe and Mail and The Canadian Press, sued Anthropic in Ontario.
- 8 October: USA Today, Gannett and other US papers sued OpenAI in New York.
- 19 October: more than 200 authors filed complaints against Meta in California.
- 21 and 23 October: music companies sued Anthropic and the AI music firm Suno.

None of these new cases has been decided. In the big New York Times case against OpenAI and Microsoft, a judge has not yet ruled on the main question of 'fair use', a US legal rule that sometimes allows use of copyrighted work without permission.

Sources: Press Gazette, Copyright Alliance

articles.title: Microsoft, Amazon and Google report fast cloud growth and huge AI spending
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet, Google's parent company, reported results on 28 and 29 October 2026. Their cloud businesses grew very fast because of demand for AI, but they are also spending record amounts on data centres and chips.

## Microsoft

Microsoft reported revenue of $92.28 billion for the July to September quarter, up 19% from a year earlier, CNBC reported. Azure, its cloud service, earned $33.17 billion, up 48%. It was the first time Microsoft shared Azure's revenue in dollars, and Azure is now its biggest single business.

- Capital spending, meaning money spent on buildings and equipment such as servers, was $45.2 billion including leases.
- Chief financial officer Amy Hood said: 'We still have demand that exceeds supply.'
- Microsoft expects about $170 billion of such spending in 2027.
- Higher memory prices and weak PC demand hurt Windows sales.

CNBC also reported that Microsoft cut 4,800 jobs in the quarter and offered voluntary buyouts to up to 60,000 employees.

## Amazon

Amazon said on 29 October that its cloud business, Amazon Web Services (AWS), grew 39%, its fastest growth in nearly five years. Chief executive Andy Jassy said AWS has a backlog, meaning signed future business, of $578 billion.

'We're installing an AI accelerator about every 14 seconds,' Jassy said. An AI accelerator is a special chip for running AI.

According to several reports on the results, Amazon spent about $77 billion on capital projects in the quarter and expects around $220 billion for the full year. Its profit per share was below forecasts, and its shares fell after the report.

## Alphabet

Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to nearly $31 billion, CNBC reported. But revenue from Google Search grew 12% to about $63 billion, below what analysts expected for a second quarter in a row.

- Alphabet kept its 2026 spending plan at $195 billion to $205 billion.
- Free cash flow, the money left after spending, was negative $9 billion.
- Its shares fell about 13% on 29 October, the biggest one-day fall on record.

Google said currency changes were the main reason for slower search growth. Some analysts worried that AI chatbots may be taking users away from traditional search. Others said it was too early to judge from one quarter.

## Why it matters

The results show that demand for AI computing is still strong. But investors are increasingly worried about the cost. Much of the spending goes on short-lived equipment such as chips, which need replacing after a few years.

Sources: CNBC, Amazon

articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.title: Intel sales grow 21% as demand for data centre chips jumps
articles.body:
US chipmaker Intel reported its results for July to September 2026 on October 29. Its revenue rose 21% from a year earlier, led by strong demand for chips used in data centres.

## The main numbers

- Revenue was 16.5 billion dollars, up from 13.7 billion dollars a year earlier.
- Net income was 3.3 billion dollars, down 18%. Earnings per share were 60 cents, down 33%.
- On an adjusted basis, which leaves out some one-off items, earnings per share were 52 cents, up 126%.
- The company made 5.1 billion dollars in cash from its operations.

Earnings per share means the profit divided by the number of company shares.

## Which parts grew

Intel has several business groups:

- Data Center and AI: 7.3 billion dollars, up 78%. This group makes Xeon processors, the main chips inside many servers.
- Intel Foundry: 6.7 billion dollars, up 58%. A foundry is a factory business that makes chips, for Intel and for other companies.
- Client Computing and Physical AI: 8.1 billion dollars, down 5%. This group mainly makes chips for laptops and desktop PCs.

Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said: "Our Q3 results demonstrate improving execution." He said demand for Intel's processors remains strong and that the first goal is to make more Xeon chips to meet demand.

## Other news in the report

- Intel released an early design kit for its future "14A" chipmaking process. Design kits help other companies plan chips for Intel's factories.
- It announced work with Dutch company ASML on "High-NA EUV", a very advanced machine that prints tiny patterns on chips.
- It agreed a multi-year deal with Oracle to offer more Xeon-based services in Oracle's cloud.
- It mentioned a 23-billion-dollar public share sale and a plan to buy a company called Classiq.

## What comes next

For October to December 2026, Intel expects revenue of between 15 billion and 16 billion dollars. That is a little lower than the third quarter. It also expects lower profit margins in the fourth quarter.

Sources: Intel (official results release), US SEC filing

articles.title: 'Dawn of Yemen': Saudi-Backed Forces Push Back Against the Houthis
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
In early October 2026, Yemen's government started a big military operation called "Dawn of Yemen" against the Houthis. Saudi Arabia supports it with heavy air strikes. The stated goal is to take back all Houthi-held land, including the capital, Sanaa.

Yemen has two main sides. The internationally recognised government is led by the Presidential Leadership Council, whose chairman is Rashad al-Alimi. The Houthis, a group backed by Iran, have held Sanaa since 2014.

## Why the operation started

In September 2026, the Houthis moved fast and took much of Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the port of Mocha, and the area near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a narrow sea route for world shipping. Analysts told Al Jazeera that government forces were poorly organised and had lost the coast quickly.

Al-Alimi announced "Dawn of Yemen" on October 5. He said it aims to retake all remaining Houthi territory, "including the capital, Sanaa."

## Who is fighting

- The Saudi-led coalition said 100 fighter jets took part at the start. It was the first air campaign the coalition acknowledged since a 2022 truce.
- The Giants Brigades, a Yemeni force first trained by the United Arab Emirates and now backed by Saudi Arabia, lead fighting on the Red Sea coast.
- A US official said 200 US military advisers are in Saudi Arabia, and US intelligence supports the campaign.
- The UK said it would give Saudi Arabia defensive support.

## What has changed on the ground

On October 5, government forces said they had retaken Mocha. Yemen's information minister, Moammar al-Eryani, told Reuters that forces had "effective control" of the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

Fighting has also spread to Marib, al-Jawf and Taiz. Taiz is a city the Houthis have surrounded for years. By mid-October, a military spokesperson claimed 1,879 strikes and said 950 Houthi fighters had been "neutralised". These numbers come from one side and cannot be checked independently.

Sanaa was hit by air strikes in mid-October and again around October 26. Before this, the city had mostly been spared bombing since 2023. As of early November, there are no reports that Sanaa has changed hands. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera doubted that the government could retake the capital soon. They said its forces must not only advance but also hold the ground they take.

## Civilians caught in the middle

In Taiz, a rights group said Houthi shelling killed five civilians and wounded 17 in one 24-hour period in October. Each side blames the other for many attacks on civilians, and most claims cannot be checked.

Sources: Al Jazeera, Reuters, Khaleej Times, FDD's Long War Journal

articles.title: US Sanctions Rwanda’s Defence Ministry Over Support for Congo Rebels
articles.body:
On October 28, 2026, the United States put sanctions on Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and a Rwandan savings bank. The US says they support the M23 rebel group, which is fighting in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Rwanda denies backing M23.

## What the US did

The US Treasury (finance ministry) sanctioned two targets:

- Rwanda's Ministry of Defence, for helping the Rwanda Defence Force, the country's army. The US had already sanctioned the army itself on March 2, 2026.
- Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a Rwandan financial institution. The US says one of its branches helped move gold from rebel-held areas to Rwanda's capital, Kigali, and handled tens of millions of dollars for M23 and its political wing.

Sanctions usually block a target's property in the United States and stop Americans from doing business with it.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said: "Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC."

## The conflict

M23 is an armed group that has fought on and off in eastern Congo for years. In early 2025 it captured Goma and Bukavu, the main cities of North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. It also controls mining areas, including gold mines and Rubaya, a large source of coltan, a mineral used in phones and computers.

The US says Rwanda has sent thousands of soldiers to fight alongside M23 and has given it weapons, equipment and training. It says Rwanda has also brought in anti-aircraft missiles and jamming equipment, which could put civilian planes at risk. The US statement also reports killings, illegal detentions, torture and forced labour in areas held by M23.

## A peace deal that has not stopped the fighting

The presidents of the DRC and Rwanda signed the US-brokered Washington Accords on December 4, 2025. The deal included a peace framework and an economic plan for trade, investment and minerals in the region. Separately, the DRC government and M23 signed a framework in Doha, Qatar, in November 2025.

But fighting has continued in North and South Kivu. A UN Security Council report in September said key steps under the Washington process were still not complete. Bessent linked the new sanctions to President Trump's promise to hold Rwanda to its promises under the accords.

## What comes next

On October 29, Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi asked Russia, a permanent member of the UN Security Council, to support peace efforts with Rwanda, according to the Rio Times. Rwanda has called earlier US sanctions unjust.

Sources: US Treasury (via Eurasia Review), The Citizen (Kenya), The Observer (Uganda), Rio Times, Security Council Report
articles.author: Digest Editors

articles.title: Global Economy: Oil Shock Pushes US Rates Up as IMF Sees Slower Growth
articles.body:
On October 28, 2026, the US Federal Reserve kept its main interest rate at 3.75% to 4%. This came after the Fed raised rates in September for the first time in more than three years, because high fuel prices pushed inflation up.

## Why rates went up

The Federal Reserve, or "the Fed", is the US central bank. It raises interest rates to slow rising prices (inflation) and cuts them to support growth.

On September 16, the Fed raised its rate by 0.25 percentage points. US prices were rising at 3.4% a year in August, well above the Fed's 2% target. The war between the US, Israel and Iran pushed up energy prices. In mid-September, Brent crude oil, the world's main oil price, was near $109 a barrel. US diesel fuel hit a record $6.31 a gallon, about double its price a year earlier.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the Fed cannot control the price of oil or food, but it can try to stop higher prices from spreading to the whole economy.

## A split vote in October

In October, the Fed decided to wait. Ten members voted to keep rates the same. Two, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, wanted another increase. The Fed said inflation "remains elevated." Economists worry that price rises have spread beyond energy. Financial markets expect a possible hike at the next meeting on December 9.

Higher US rates matter around the world. They make borrowing more expensive for governments, companies and families, and can weaken other currencies against the dollar. In September, the interest rate on 10-year US government bonds passed 5%, the highest in 19 years, and US mortgage rates rose above 7%.

President Donald Trump has publicly demanded much lower rates.

## The IMF's view

On October 13, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which advises governments on their economies, published its World Economic Outlook. The title was "Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices." It said:

- World growth will slow to 3.1% in 2026, from 3.5% in 2025, then recover to 3.4% in 2027.
- Global inflation will rise to 4.7% in 2026 and ease to 4.1% in 2027.
- Rich economies will grow about 2.1% this year and developing economies about 3.7%.
- The euro area will grow only 1.1%, while India will grow about 7%.

The IMF said energy-importing countries outside the technology industry face the hardest outlook. It said the main risks are worse conflicts, renewed trade tensions, high government debt, and a possible fall in expectations about artificial intelligence (AI). Stronger AI investment and fewer trade tensions could help growth.

Sources: CNBC, Al Jazeera, International Monetary Fund, NPR, Yahoo Finance

articles.title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Argon and a Restricted Cyber-Security Model, Carbon
articles.body:
Google released a new top AI model, Gemini 4 Argon, on 13 October 2026. Two weeks later, on 28 October, it announced an even stronger model, Gemini 4 Carbon, but it is giving Carbon only to a small group of security experts for now.

## Gemini 4 Argon

Google calls Argon its latest "frontier" model. A frontier model is one of the most advanced AI systems available. Google says Argon is better at long tasks with many steps, such as coding, finance, legal work and science. It also says Argon writes more directly and follows instructions better.

Argon is available around the world:

- for developers and businesses through Google's AI Studio and its API (a way for software to connect to the model);
- in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in Google Search for paying Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

Developers pay an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. A "token" is a small piece of text, about part of a word. From 30 November 2026 the price rises to $4 and $20.

Google says Argon was tested under its Frontier Safety Framework, its set of rules for checking dangerous abilities before release.

## Gemini 4 Carbon

Google describes Carbon as "our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities". "Long horizon" means it can keep working on a long task for a long time. Google says internal teams have seen it work for days on big software projects.

Carbon is very good at finding weaknesses in computer code. Google reports these test scores:

- 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, a test of finding security holes;
- 71.0% on CWE-bench, a test of fixing them.

## Why access is limited

Tools that find security holes can help defenders fix them, but they could also help attackers. For this reason, Google is first giving Carbon to a group of "cyber defenders" and will slowly add more trusted partners through a programme called Fairwind. Google says it is also taking part in the US government's voluntary testing of models before release. It has not given a date for wider public access.

The release comes during strong competition between Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and other labs to build the most capable models.

Sources: Google Blog, Google Cloud Blog, TechCrunch

articles.title: Memory chip shortage brings record profits for chipmakers and higher prices for devices
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
South Korean chipmaker SK hynix reported the biggest profit in its history on October 28, 2026. The company also warned that the world will not have enough memory chips until 2030. The shortage is making phones, computers and game consoles more expensive.

## What memory chips do

Memory chips store data while a device is working. DRAM is the main type used in phones, PCs and servers. HBM (high-bandwidth memory) is a special, very fast type used in the powerful computers that run artificial intelligence. Building HBM uses much more factory capacity than normal memory. So when chipmakers make more HBM for AI data centres, less normal memory is left for consumer devices.

## Record results

SK hynix said its operating profit in July to September was 83.3 trillion won (about $62 billion). That is 632% more than a year earlier. Its sales passed 100 trillion won in one quarter for the first time. The company said average DRAM prices rose by more than 25% compared with the previous three months. It expects demand to be higher than supply "through 2030". It says new factories take a long time to build and the newest chips are technically difficult to make.

Samsung Electronics, the world's other big memory maker, said on October 8 that it expected a record operating profit of about 107.4 trillion won for the same quarter. Reuters reported that Samsung and US company Micron both expect memory supply to stay tight until 2028.

## Higher prices for buyers

SK hynix's finance chief said he expects fewer PCs and phones to be sold because memory is more expensive. Several companies have already raised prices in 2026:

- Nintendo raised the US price of the Switch 2 from $449.99 to $499.99 from September 1, with increases in other regions too.
- Microsoft raised Xbox console prices worldwide from August 1, saying memory and storage costs had gone up.
- Apple raised the prices of some iPhone models at its September launch.

Research firm Counterpoint expected the average price of a smartphone to rise in 2026. Some analysts say the shortage could ease when new factories open, as in past chip cycles. But for now, chipmakers are signing long contracts with big cloud companies. SK hynix said deals with 14 major customers already cover more than half of its production for 2027 and 2028.

Sources: The Next Web, TrendForce, Seoul Economic Daily, Korea Times, TechSpot

articles.title: UAE's G42 signs AI deals in Greece and says UAE can export 'intelligence'
articles.author: Digest Editors
articles.body:
G42, a large technology group based in Abu Dhabi, signed several agreements in Greece on 23 October 2026. Three days later, at the Dubai AI Festival, its chief executive said the UAE wants to move from exporting energy to exporting 'intelligence'.

## Deals in Greece

The agreements were signed in Athens during an official visit by Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, at the UAE-Greece Strategic Forum. In total, the two countries signed 18 agreements and partnerships worth 12.75 billion euros ($14.3 billion), according to The National. G42's deals are part of this package. They are early-stage agreements to explore projects, not final contracts.

- Khazna Data Centres and Core42, two G42 companies, will work with Greece's Copelouzos Group to explore building an 'AI factory', a large data centre for AI. It would serve banks, telecoms, shipping and government.
- Presight will work with Greece's Ministry of Digital Governance on AI for city services, starting with waste management and water network monitoring.
- Inception42 plans to use AI agents in government and education, including AI tutors. AI agents are programs that can carry out tasks step by step, not only answer questions.
- M42, a health company, signed a pact with Athens LifeTech Park on genomics (the study of DNA) and medical research.

Mansoor Al Mansoori, CEO of G42 International, said the deals 'mark an important milestone in expanding G42's intelligence grid across Europe.'

## 'From energy exporter to intelligence exporter'

On 26 October, G42's group CEO Peng Xiao spoke at the Dubai AI Festival. 'I think our ambition is to go from an energy exporter to become an intelligence exporter,' he said. He argued that the UAE's reliable energy and fast building of computing centres could help it sell AI services to the world.

G42 is building a 5-gigawatt AI campus in Abu Dhabi. It includes Stargate UAE, a 1-gigawatt project with OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia, Cisco and SoftBank. Xiao said many American partners are now coming to the region for computing power, and that the UAE's location could let it serve about 4 billion potential users.

## Government reviews AI plans more often

Omar Al Olama, the UAE Minister of State for AI, spoke at the same event. He said UAE leaders now review their AI plans every six months, instead of once a year. He told workers to see AI as a tool that multiplies their work, but also warned that 'there is going to be disruption on the horizon' for companies and governments.

He noted that in April 2026, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, launched a plan to use AI agents in 50% of federal government sectors within two years.

Sources: The National, G42

articles.title: Brazil: Lula Wins a Record Fourth Term in Surprise Comeback
articles.body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff on October 25, 2026. He beat right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro and will serve a fourth term as president, something no Brazilian leader has done before.

## A close and surprising result

Brazil, the largest country in Latin America, held the first round of voting on October 4. Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, came first with about 47% of the vote. Lula had about 45%. Almost all final polls before the runoff showed Bolsonaro slightly ahead.

But in the second round, Lula won about 51.8% against 48.2% for Bolsonaro, a lead of more than 4 million votes. According to AP, it is the first time since 1985 that the candidate who came second in the first round went on to win the presidency.

Lula, a left-wing politician, will soon be 81 years old. His new term begins on January 5, 2027.

## What voters cared about

- Cost of living: Bolsonaro promised lower food prices.
- Crime and security: Bolsonaro campaigned on tough policies against crime.
- The United States: Lula is a strong critic of US President Donald Trump, who put tariffs (import taxes) on Brazilian goods. Lula said a Bolsonaro government would let the US control Brazil.

Both campaigns faced questions about corruption involving family members and allies. On election day, a Supreme Court judge extended voting by two hours, at the request of both campaigns.

## Challenges ahead

Bolsonaro claimed there were irregularities and said he would challenge the result. Experts quoted by Americas Quarterly said this would be very difficult because of the size of Lula's lead. Several regional leaders quickly recognised Lula's victory.

Lula will also face a difficult Congress. Analysts describe it as the most conservative Congress in Brazil's recent history, and the Senate will be hostile to many of his plans.

The economy is another problem. Analysts say the government's deficit (the gap between spending and income) is close to 10% of the size of the economy after heavy spending before the election. Financial markets fell after the result. Economists say Lula needs to name a trusted finance minister quickly and present a clear plan for public money.

## Why it matters

Brazil is a major world food and energy producer. Some analysts see Lula's win as a counterweight in a region where several countries have recently elected right-wing leaders.

Sources: AP/PBS NewsHour, Americas Quarterly, NPR, Bloomberg
